---
title: "renv::install() ignores the repository written in the lockfile"
ref: RNV-01
categories: [renv and installation]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "packages taken from the dated repository of the lockfile"
versions: "Observed with {renv} 1.2.4"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2026)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```text
renv.lock:
  "R": {
    "Version": "4.6.1",
    "Repositories": [
      { "Name": "CRAN", "URL": "https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-09-01" }
    ]
  }

> getOption("repos")
                       CRAN
"https://cran.rstudio.com"
```

```r
renv::install("xfun")
renv::snapshot()
```
:::

This pitfall depends on a {renv} project, remote repositories and the network, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

The repository recorded in the lockfile is not the one `renv::install()` uses: it takes `getOption("repos")`. When the project loads, {renv} normally replaces that option with the lockfile repositories, unless it is redefined elsewhere, for instance in an `Rprofile.site`, a `.Rprofile` or an option set by hand.

The package is then installed from current CRAN, not from the dated snapshot. At the next `snapshot()`, the lockfile records the active repository: the dated address disappears from the file, and with it the reproducibility it guaranteed.

## The remedy

Check `getOption("repos")` before installing, and do not redefine the repositories in a {renv} project unless you mean to.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
getOption("repos")
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-09-01"))
renv::install("xfun")
renv::snapshot()
```
:::
